query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing coherent nanoprecipitations through a stepwise thermo-mechanical process can improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries
generation.intervention: Stepwise thermo-mechanical process with coherent nanoprecipitations
generation.mechanism: The coherent interfaces of the nanoprecipitations facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, while the nanoprecipitations themselves provide order hardening and lattice misfit strengthening, leading to improved strength and ductility. This mechanism is derived from materials-science principles and supported by the transferable evidence from record PMC10213035 and partially transferable evidence from records PMC4145285 and PMC7514651.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and room-temperature tensile ductility
generation.boundary: Limited to eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of coherent nanoprecipitation formation and its effect on dislocation mobility is still unclear

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile tests at room temperature on eutectic high-entropy alloys with and without coherent nanoprecipitations
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with coherent nanoprecipitations does not show improved strength and ductility compared to the unmodified alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
